clue.text: Serbian scientist fully prepared to ditch a student on returning

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters are read from right to left
to ditch something is to throw it away, so one letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: all set means completely ready
L is a learner driver's plate, so a student; one of the two Ls goes

explanation.surface: A scientist from Serbia, ready for anything, drops a pupil on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL SET loses one L to leave ALSET, which reversed gives TESLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla, the electrical engineer and inventor, was an ethnic Serb born in what is now Croatia.

clue.text: Officer giving suggestion to senior officer's group

parts.note: a tip is a hint or suggestion
a general's staff is the group of officers serving under him

explanation.surface: A junior officer passes a hint to the team around a commanding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a court officer, originally one carrying a metal-tipped staff of office.

clue.text: Nasty character putting oar in about love

parts.note: a scull is a type of oar

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: taken as written; it wraps around the next piece
love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A rower sticks an oar in, and the result is somebody unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting oar in' looks like an insertion signal, but the pieces simply run in order, with only love sitting inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullion was a kitchen drudge, and the word came to mean a base, contemptible person.

clue.text: Tree area rising, becoming adequate

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means moving to the top, so one letter is lifted out and placed first

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
a maple is a tree; its A moves up

explanation.surface: A wooded patch grows until it is big enough.
explanation.walkthrough: In MAPLE the A (area) rises to the top of the down light, giving A + MPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means enough or more than enough, a close synonym of sufficient.

clue.text: Traditional girl, one attending college in California

indicators.note: being in a place means sitting inside it, so the girl and the rest go within the state

parts.note: Cal is the short form of California
a lass is a girl
Roman numeral one
C is a common abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned young woman is studying at a Californian college.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical describes established, conventional forms, so it can stand for traditional.

clue.text: Treatment for unwanted growth repaired torn carpels

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together differently, so these letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A botanist mends damaged flower parts to stop an unwanted growth.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpels and 'unwanted growth' suggest gardening, but the growth is a corn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn plaster is a medicated pad applied to a corn, a hard thickening of skin on the foot.

clue.text: Atmosphere in flight shunned by holy man

indicators.note: what is shunned is kept away, so those letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: a flight of stairs; STAIR stands in for it
ST, saint, is a holy man; these letters go

explanation.surface: The cabin air on a plane is avoided by a religious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests aircraft; it is a set of steps, STAIR, from which ST is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Air is the gaseous envelope around us, and atmosphere also means a prevailing mood or air.

clue.text: Twirling sticks carried by band from England

indicators.note: carried by means held within, so the twirled sticks sit inside the band

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist

indicators.note: twirling turns something around, so the sticks are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: canes are walking sticks

explanation.surface: A marching band from England twirls batons as it parades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but it is a strip of cloth worn across the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassenach is a Scots and Irish word for an English person, also used adjectivally for English.

clue.text: Large part of work — nearly the entirety — requiring singers

indicators.note: a large part is most but not all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a chore is a piece of work; its final letter goes

indicators.note: nearly falls just short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: all is the whole amount; its final letter goes

explanation.surface: Most of a musical work, almost the whole thing, needs a chorus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' suggests a musical composition, but it is a household chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral music is written for a choir, so it needs a body of voices to perform it.

clue.text: Songs? Prominent violinist is what's heard

indicators.note: what is heard points to the spoken sound of a word rather than its spelling

parts.note: the principal first violinist of an orchestra is its leader

explanation.surface: A question about songs and the orchestra's star violinist.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage the leader of an orchestra is the principal first violin (Americans say concertmaster).
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs for voice and piano, as written by Schubert and Schumann.

clue.text: One choosing to be more obese?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who plumps for something, deciding on it
second meaning: the comparative of a word for chubby

explanation.surface: Someone who decides to put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: To plump for something is to choose it, so a plumper is a chooser; the same letters compare two fat people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an agent noun from the idiom plump for and the comparative of an adjective meaning fat.

clue.text: Fried food recipe is fish

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin 'take' on prescriptions
taken as written
sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction declaring the fried dish to be fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a small fried cake of minced meat or fish coated in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: Recalled correction about line in diacritical mark

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the correction is read backwards
about means surrounding, so the line is held inside

parts.note: an edit is a correction to a text
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A proofreader withdraws an amendment concerning a stroke in an accent.
explanation.walkthrough: EDIT reversed is TIDE, which then goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilde is the wavy accent placed over a letter, as in Spanish ñ.

clue.text: Map feature in Nepal came misrepresented

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown in a distorted form, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cartographer's error: something shown in Nepal turned out wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Maps are labelled with the names of towns and features, each one a place name.

clue.text: I'm USA caper, possibly, around cold water? But NZ are the holders!

definitions.text: water? But NZ are the holders!

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the reworked letters surround the cold
possibly suggests one arrangement among several, so these letters may be shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An American boasts of a watery escapade, only to be reminded that New Zealand hold the trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of I'M USA CAPER are rearranged around C. New Zealand held the trophy when this was set.
explanation.definitionFit: The America's Cup is the famous yachting trophy contested on water, which New Zealand's team has won repeatedly.

clue.text: Servant carrying silverware? One's stoked

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a footman is a liveried household servant
plate is household silver or gilt dishes

explanation.surface: A butler's assistant carries the family silver, and someone is fired up.
explanation.walkthrough: A footman carrying plate is a natural picture, which hides that the definition is about steam engines; read 'One's stoked' as 'one who has stoked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A footplateman is a railway engine driver or fireman, who worked on the locomotive's footplate stoking the firebox.

clue.text: Poet's lies reinterpreted as a matter of good manners

indicators.note: reinterpreted means given a new reading, so these letters are arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet's fibs are explained away as mere courtesy.
explanation.definitionFit: Politesse, borrowed from French, is formal politeness or etiquette.

clue.text: Official upset over urban savagery

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down entry reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a ref, referee, is a sports official
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
city as a modifier, as in city life, means urban

explanation.surface: A referee is angry about violence in the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suggests annoyance, but in a down light it turns the official's word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferocity is fierce, savage violence, so it serves as a synonym of savagery.

clue.text: Is French movement set apart?

parts.note: est is French for is
range of movement is the extent something can move

explanation.surface: A question whether a French artistic movement stands apart from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French movement' reads as an art school, but 'French' belongs with 'Is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate or separate people who were once close.

clue.text: Lust she isn't distributing — just a bit of slovenly debauchery?

indicators.note: distributing spreads things about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: just a bit of something means only a small piece, here its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of slovenly

explanation.surface: A woman withholding her desires, with a hint of sloppy depravity.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluttishness is an old-fashioned word for slovenliness or loose sexual morals, hence debauchery; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Disgusted comments on the rise in sandstorm

indicators.note: on the rise means going upward, which in a down entry reads the letters from the bottom

parts.note: boo and bah are two exclamations of disgust

explanation.surface: Grumbles grow louder as a sandstorm blows up.
explanation.walkthrough: BOO and BAH together are reversed upwards to give HABOOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A haboob is a violent dust storm of Sudan and other desert regions, borrowed from Arabic.

clue.text: Foil wrapping tail of bird in TV promotion

indicators.note: wrapping means enclosing, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to foil something is to avert or prevent it

indicators.note: a tail is the hindmost part, so only the end letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of bird

explanation.surface: Tin foil is wrapped round a bird's tail feathers for a television commercial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' looks like kitchen foil, but it is a verb meaning to thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is a commercial, the short promotional break shown on television.

clue.text: Assessor of accounts backed excellent performance spaces

parts.note: an auditor checks a firm's accounts

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the word for excellent is read in reverse

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written with the letter I standing for 1

explanation.surface: An auditor supports some outstanding concert venues.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first-rate, appears as AI and reversed gives IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditoria is the Latin plural of auditorium, the hall where an audience watches a performance.

clue.text: Love in the morning for us

parts.note: a.m. denotes the morning
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: Romance before noon is just right for the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is French for love, used in English for a romance or love affair.

clue.text: Allow a daughter to attend US institute

parts.note: taken as written
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Parents let their daughter go to study at an American university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to attend' reads as part of the picture but just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in, so it can mean permit or allow.

clue.text: Deliveries dispatched overlooking new disorder

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler

indicators.note: overlooking something means leaving it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: sent means dispatched
N is the abbreviation for new; it is dropped

explanation.surface: Parcels were sent out ignoring the latest chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests the post; in cricket a bowler's deliveries make up overs.
explanation.definitionFit: Overset is an older verb meaning upset or overturn, so to throw into disorder.

clue.text: Response in an instant on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard and not seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: A quick reply delivered live over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Response' is a stretch: a tic is an involuntary twitch, a reflex response.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is an involuntary muscular spasm, a kind of automatic reaction of the body.

clue.text: Fictional detective: a married investigator probing swindle

indicators.note: something probing goes inside, so those pieces are placed within the swindle

parts.note: a con is a swindle
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for married
a PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A sleuth from fiction, with a wedded private eye, looks into a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Campion is the gentleman sleuth in Margery Allingham's mystery novels.

clue.text: Flannel enclosing cold flower

indicators.note: enclosing means surrounding, so the cold goes inside the other phrase

parts.note: flannel is smooth flattery, which is to butter up
C is the abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A face cloth wrapped around a chilly bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: A flannel is also a British face cloth; here it is the verb, to flatter.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow wild flower of the genus Ranunculus.

clue.text: Returned surprised comment, captivated by the flavouring

indicators.note: captivated suggests being held captive, so the exclamation sits inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone sends back a startled remark, charmed by the seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' looks like a mere article in the surface, but it supplies the outer letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic herb used to season food.
